newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK August retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK August retail sales data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to data showing UK August retail sales rose 1.0 percent month on month and 4.4 percent year on year.
The consensus forecast was for a month on month rise of 0.5 percent and a year on year increase of 3.5 percent.
"I think the figure is slightly negative for gilts and short sterling. Strength in retail sales could be due to strong households goods and clothing and footwear sales."

"Strong figures confirming that the economy is experiencing a rebound in consumer spending and fitting in with the message from recent CBI surveys. It's important to stress though that this does not imply any immediate inflation threat. The economy will be able to experience stronger growth and continued low inflation. Thus the Bank of England's call for a rate hike as seen in the minutes is still premature."

"Very impressive figures indeed. The risks were always on the upside but I don't think anyone would have gone for this much of a rise. It indicates the consumer is finally turning the corner, but its negative for the gilt market on the back of the Bank of England looking for a rate rise already. We're already seeing the gilt market suffer and this could continue for a few days as these figures filter through."
